newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-NAPOLI'S SIMONI IS SEVENTH SERIE A SACKING.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-NAPOLI'S SIMONI IS SEVENTH SERIE A SACKING.

text.p: Napoli coach Luigi Simoni, who moves to Inter next season, on Monday became the seventh serie A coach to lose his job when the Italian Cup finalists sacked him.
"Napoli has decided to dismiss coach Luigi Simoni," the southern club said in a terse statement after an emergency meeting of club officials earlier in the day.
"The team has been entrusted to Vincenzo Montefusco. Napoli thanks Simoni for the work he has carried out."
Montefusco is Napoli's junior team coach.
Despite getting Napoli to the two-leg final of the Italian Cup, against Vicenza next month, few had expected Simoni to last out the season at the club despite his repeatedly expressed desire to stay.
Simoni was clearly upset at being denied a chance of attending the first cup final of his career.
"Maybe I should have lied," he told the Italian news agency Ansa about his deal with Inter which Massimo Moratti, the president of the Milanese club, has confirmed openly.
"I'm disappointed, I didn't think it would come to this after two bad games. Napoli are not last in the table and still have the cup final ahead."
"I have never played a cup final as a coach. I thought I had earned it and instead they have prevented me."
Simoni said he spoke to club president Corrado Ferlaino last Thursday who gave him no hint of trouble.
"I did not have any particular problems at Napoli," he insisted. "Maybe there are other motives behind this sacking."
Relations between the coach and his employers, already soured after his contacts with Inter became public knowledge, have gone from bad to worse in recent weeks.
The last straw was a 1-0 defeat at home by Atalanta on Sunday which sent Napoli to 13th place in the league. It was the first time Atalanta had won at Napoli in 41 years.

The financially strapped southerners, a pale shadow of the once great club that with Argentine Diego Maradona won the league title in 1987 and 1990 as well as the UEFA Cup in 1989, have not won a match for three months.

Commentators agreed that Sunday's game was one of their worst performances of the season and fans vented their rage against the 58-year-old coach and Brazilian defender Andre Cruz who is reportedly set to join him at Inter.
Simoni was approached by Inter after English coach Roy Hodgson announced he was leaving at the end of the season to take over at English club Blackburn.
Ironically, of the coaches who had been considered to be in the running for Hodgson's job, Simoni's team has performed worst of all since the negotiations started.
